title: The pawn: moves and captures are different
outcomes: Taps every square a pawn can move to, including the two-square start and diagonal captures
Knows a pawn cannot capture straight ahead and is blocked by any piece in front of it
Knows what happens when a pawn reaches the last rank

steps.text: **Pawns** move straight forward, one square at a time, and never backward. From their starting square they may move two squares if both are empty. But pawns **capture** differently: one square diagonally forward. A pawn cannot capture straight ahead, and any piece directly in front of it blocks it.

steps.caption: Forward to e3 or e4, or a capture on d3. The pawn goes diagonally only to capture.

steps.text: Two details cause most pawn mistakes. The two-square jump is only for a pawn's first move, and only if both squares are empty. And a pawn captures diagonally, never straight ahead. Before moving a pawn ask: has it moved yet? And is the square ahead empty?

steps.title: Same pawn, one change
steps.prompt: The pawn moves up one square to e3. Predict first: can it still jump two squares?

steps.title: Same pawn, a different target
steps.prompt: The knight steps from the diagonal to straight ahead. Predict first: can the pawn still capture it?

steps.caption: When a pawn reaches the last rank, it turns into a new piece. Here it becomes a queen.

line.say: The pawn reaches e8 and becomes a queen.
